(i) irpt-ycharts-generate WAS protected, and by the strongest thing in the project: job.lambda_handler reads Andrew's per-use consent from the environment and REFUSES a live YCharts call outright. A browser request reaching it got that refusal -- a correct sentence about the wrong question. GUARDING CHANGED THE PROTECTION'S SHAPE AND MADE IT STRONGER: the request half is now a separate entry that never touches the vendor at all, so there is no path from an HTTP request to a YCharts call to gate; the queue half keeps its consent gate UNCHANGED and is still what the irpt-generation queue drives. The gate was not relaxed, removed or duplicated. (ii) irpt-export-render WAS protected by an ABSENT OPERATION: there was no export-status read, so the route answered the controller's capabilities blob. Guarding ADDED the operation, which is a new reachable surface -- so the protection that came from absence is gone and is replaced by an explicit one: the receipt key's firm segment is built from the VERIFIED principal, so a caller holding another firm's export id reads a key that does not exist rather than another firm's receipt, and that check sits BELOW the scope check rather than instead of it. submit-export is deliberately NOT wired to the controller (another cell is changing it this window) and refuses NOT_READY. (iii) irpt-narrative and irpt-performance-adapter were protected by NOTHING, and both were worse than unguarded: each read the viewer's scope OUT OF THE REQUEST. performance passes resolved_scope.scope_ids to the vendor AS THE CALCULATION'S ACCOUNT SET, so a caller-supplied scope was a caller-supplied CALCULATION, not merely a caller-supplied filter; narrative built a packet from a report the request supplied, so even a guarded caller could hand in another firm's report. Guarding closed both, and narrative needed BOTH halves -- the guard authorizes the CALLER and the object arrives in the request. (iv) irpt-directory-search was protected by its own projection rules, which are correct and enforce nothing while the caller supplies the scope they filter by.
